findings.title: disable_user lacks the last-admin guard that delete_user has, and no re-enable route exists — an admin can irreversibly brick all admin capability
findings.description: delete_user (admin.rs:98-120) explicitly refuses to remove the last active admin via db.count_active_admins() (<= 1 => Conflict). disable_user (admin.rs:68-80) has no equivalent check: it will disable any user id, including the only/last remaining admin account, and then calls revoke_all_sessions_for_user. Because SessionAuth rejects any user whose disabled_at is set (session_auth.rs:202-208) and the AdminUser extractor requires role.is_admin() on a live session, once the last admin is disabled there is no authenticated admin left. Critically, the admin API exposes only list/create/disable/reset-password/delete users (routes.rs:612-616) — there is NO re-enable endpoint — so this state is not recoverable through the API and requires direct database surgery.
findings.attackOrTrigger: An authenticated admin issues POST /api/admin/users/{id}/disable targeting the only admin account (which may be their own id). The request succeeds, the admin's sessions are revoked, and every subsequent admin-gated call (user management at /api/admin/*, backup list/create/restore/delete at /api/backups*) returns 401/403 for everyone. No API path can restore an admin.
findings.why: It is a real, user-impacting correctness/availability gap with an obvious intended-but-missing guard: the sibling delete_user path guards exactly this condition, showing the invariant 'at least one active admin must always exist' was meant to hold. It is not a privilege escalation (only a trusted admin can trigger it) and is not remotely exploitable, so it is not high/critical, but the irreversibility via API elevates it above a trivial footgun.
findings.fixSketch: Before disabling, if the target user's role is admin, call db.count_active_admins() and reject with Conflict when it is <= 1 (mirror the guard in delete_user). Optionally also refuse to disable one's own account, and/or add an enable_user route so the state is recoverable.
